Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Pullman Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors of America, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; directs that, in performing its functions under the order, the board comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Pullman Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10286 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). The report deadline and the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C); because no report date can be read, no functionally-spent date is recorded, and the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The PDF page images are not held in the repository, so a page check of the report is the missing source for a report date. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order.
